author: Taras Pasternak

steps.title: Import raw images into Fiji
steps.instruction: Open Fiji, choose Plugins → Bio‑Formats → Bio‑Formats Importer, select all relevant .lsm or .tiff series, and click OK.

steps.title: Export images to HDF5
steps.instruction: In Fiji, select Plugins → HDF5 → Save to HDF5 and choose to create a new file or replace an existing one.

steps.title: Stitch image tiles
steps.instruction: Stitch tiles using the recommended XUV‑tool or, alternatively, Fiji 3D stitching.

substeps.instruction: XUV‑tool: Add files to the project, select the tiles to stitch, run the stitcher, ignore current coordinates, click Run, then Save as .hdf5 (do NOT use “Save project”; default is .ims). When stitching multiple channels, first save tile positions from the first channel (Position Editor → note positions) and reuse them for subsequent channels.

Fiji 3D stitching (alternative): Plugins → Stitching → deprecated → 3D Stitching, select the first and second series, click OK, then repeat by selecting the combined series and the next series until all series are stitched. Note that this method only stitches two tiles at a time and requires higher memory.

steps.title: Load HDF5 file into iRoCS
steps.instruction: In iRoCS, go to Channel → Import Channels, select the HDF5 file, and choose t0/channel0 as the channel to load.

steps.title: Segment root structure
steps.instruction: Run Plugins → C01 Segment root; set the processing element size to a value between 0.5 and 0.7 for reasonable runtime, and adjust gamma correction between 1 and 2 according to image quality.

steps.title: Clean segmentation artifacts
steps.instruction: Optionally remove irrelevant segments and correct over‑segmented cells.

substeps.instruction: Hold Shift, right‑click on black background, then left‑click on any segment to delete it.
Hold Ctrl, right‑click on a fragment, move the cursor to the fragment you wish to fuse, and left‑click to merge.

steps.title: Add QC annotation marker
steps.instruction: Create a new annotation channel via Channels → New annotation channel, place a point at the QC location, and optionally rename the channel to “QC”.

steps.title: Attach iRoCS coordinate axis
steps.instruction: Select Plugins → C02 Attach iRoCS to segmented cells, choose the segmentation/cellular Masks channel as the segmentation input and the previously created QC channel as the QC input.

steps.title: Convert mask to cell markers
steps.instruction: Run the Connected Component Labeling plugin, choose “cells” as the marker type, and start processing.

steps.title: Assign cell layers
steps.instruction: Assign layers to segmented cells using either the Arabidopsis model or manual settings.

substeps.instruction: Arabidopsis root: Plugins → C03 Assign layers to segmented cell, load the model files downloaded from the iRoCS website, and click OK.

Other organs: In the Channel Control window, move “/cellularMasks” and then “/annotation/segmented” to visible, set View type to “label”, Operation to “label marker”, open Marker Presets, choose a label marker design, and assign the desired cell type.

steps.title: Label subtypes and cell files
steps.instruction: In Marker Presets, select “subtype” and click the desired cells; then select “cell file” and click cells to assign cell‑file numbers.

steps.title: Export segmentation results
steps.instruction: Channel → Export annotation channel to CSV to save the segmentation data.

steps.title: Load HDF5 for nuclei detection
steps.instruction: Again, go to Channel → Import Channels, select the HDF5 file, and choose t0/channel0.

steps.title: Detect nuclei
steps.instruction: Run Plugins → 01 Detect Nuclei and load the appropriate model file from the iRoCS website.

steps.title: Label epidermal cells
steps.instruction: Use Plugin → 02 Label Epidermis, loading the Arabidopsis model from the website, or manually label at least 50 randomly chosen epidermal cells.

steps.title: Add QC marker for nuclei
steps.instruction: Create a QC annotation channel as described in step 7.

steps.title: Attach axis for nuclei data
steps.instruction: Plugins → 03 Attach iRoCS, select the annotation/detector channel as the annotation input and the QC channel as the QC input.

steps.title: Assign layers to nuclei
steps.instruction: Plugins → 04, load the model file (https://lmb.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/lmbsoft/iRoCS/wt-model.rf.h5) and the corresponding “Layer assignment” file.

steps.title: Manually correct layers and nuclei
steps.instruction: If image quality, plant age, or species differ, open the annotation channel, select the label marker, and manually adjust layer and nuclei labels as needed.

steps.title: Render 3D visualization
steps.instruction: View → Show OpenGL rendering; use plugin version 1.2.1 for segmented objects and version 1.2.4 for nuclei.

steps.title: Export 3D structures for printing
steps.instruction: File → Export as Analyze and STL; the plugin converts data to .stl files, grouping cells with the same label into the same file.

steps.title: Export final annotations and analyse
steps.instruction: Export annotation channels to CSV (Channel → Export annotation channel to CSV), open the files in Excel, and use columns such as X, Y, Z (center‑of‑mass), cell‑file number, distance from QC (µm), radial distance (µm), subtype, mitotic status, cell volume, nuclei radius, etc.; for root analysis also compute radians and un‑rolled coordinates for graphical presentation.

steps.title: Orient root for imaging
steps.instruction: Place the root horizontally with the tip on the left side before acquiring images.
